headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, clipboard, and supported-app content, while Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if A’s outputs are pasted or routed into B. The shared channel is not explicit, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are copied into agent_b flow inputs or files, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF agent_b treats file or flow input content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream nodes.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent_a output into agent_b flows.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-vs-data parser in the flow.
Require manual review before any agent_a-generated text reaches agent_b.
Use a separate workspace for agent_a artifacts and agent_b inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code; agent B reads server files and uploaded flow files, and B’s network egress is broad. If A’s sensitive content is fed into B, B can transmit it to arbitrary HTTP services or model providers. That is a default-dangerous exfiltration path, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs contain uploaded files, screenshots, voice, or IDE code and are passed into agent_b, sensitive data can leave the environment.
IF agent_b flows call external HTTP services with those inputs, exfiltration occurs.
mitigations: Block sensitive inputs from entering agent_b flows.
Restrict agent_b egress to an allowlist of endpoints.
Redact screenshots, voice transcripts, and code before flow ingestion.
Use separate credentials and workspaces for the two agents.
Turn off any flow step that forwards raw context to external services.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has read-only filesystem access and no write or shell, but agent B can execute shell, install packages, and write the server filesystem. If both are pointed at the same directory or shared store, B can overwrite or consume A’s artifacts without coordination. The overlap is asymmetric but still dangerous in default deployments.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a writable directory or server-side store, B can clobber or mutate A’s files.
IF agent_b flows write to paths that agent_a later reads, stale or malicious state can propagate.
mitigations: Mount separate directories for each agent.
Make shared paths read-only for agent_b.
Add file-locking or per-run namespaces.
Disable shell steps in flows that touch shared artifacts.
Snapshot inputs before agent_b writes anything.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents, and ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived outputs that B may treat as upstream inputs. Without an explicit verification gate, B can operationalize A’s mistakes into downstream actions or transformed outputs. That is a classic cascading-error pathway in default configurations.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a node input without validation, errors propagate downstream.
IF any flow node sends A-derived facts to external APIs or actions, incorrect outputs can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a verification node between agents.
Require citations or source links for any factual claim from agent_a.
Add a human approval step before external actions.
Log provenance for each field passed from A to B.
Reject uncited or low-confidence outputs from agent_a.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles screenshots, voice, uploaded files, and connected-IDE code; agent B stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs on the server. If regulated data is routed from A into B, retention and residency obligations can diverge because B’s deployment and storage model are server-side and configurable. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from agent_a is stored in agent_b server-side state, retention obligations may diverge.
IF agent_b is deployed in a different jurisdiction or retention regime than agent_a, compliance mismatch arises.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to agent_b.
Disable storage of regulated inputs in agent_b where possible.
Set explicit retention limits on flow outputs.
Use region-matched deployments for both agents.
Document a deletion/export process for shared artifacts.
